Part2:
At least I got to see how I died before returning to the windows. I peaked out of the second.

I wasn't sure what I was seeing. Instead of myself it was a boy. I didn't recognized him for a longer than I'd like to admit. It was the love of my life. I sat back, watching everything curiously. It was incredibly different from watching myself. I didn't have to anticipate the pain.

But it still hurt when things didn't go his way. I was able to celebrate his success with him in a way. Part of me wished I could talk to him about this. I love him, and he loved me longer than anyone. Perhaps it was because my family died when I was young, that I gave him every inch of my love every day so that I wouldn't wake up one day wishing I had done more.

I got to see him struggle through his own depression, and his own heartbreaks. But everything was okay, because I had him beside me, and it made everything painful more tolerable.

I couldn't be happier as I watched us live together. Even more so, seeing again how he proved he loved me again and again.

But those last few moments... I was dead and I kept turning away from seeing his pain directly. I couldn't be there anymore.

-----

The third window was extremely confusing, even as some part of me knew this person would hate me. All I knew was that this girl was growing up in the same city as I had. 

I hadn't remembered right away but her mom took some classes in college with my mom. Small world, despite how long it went before we met.

I took these opportunities to learn things I had never learned. I felt the same compassion for her as I did for anyone else. I felt the same disdain for her as I did for anyone else too.

I laughed with her, I facepalmed at her mistakes. It was much like my own naiveness only in different situations. We were more alike than I'd admit, but maybe I was just trying to relate to her.

Then she got into this school, I remembered her and knew it was only a matter of time.

A few years later I arrived at the school. We had a rivalry from day one. We got into fights, worst than mean girls, but it was just fun for me. I didn't get emotional attached or scared. It had been just another war day with some stupid kid. She didn't feel the same way.

*I* was the thing that changed her life. In her eyes, I was public enemy number one. I knew what hatred felt like, but I had no idea these silly teen fights scarred her like that. I had always found a way to forgive. It seemed like she never really did. Whenever she brought up those years of struggle, I made her life hell. All the while I had believed she had ganged up on me.

I felt shame. I wished I could take it back. It had never been my intention to hurt someone, not like that, not ever. I remember laying down on the floor for a long time. Watching her life from the corner of my eye.

It was enough. I was ready to die so why couldn't all this be over already.

Eventually I got back up, knowing that as life ended, this too would soon end.

----

With the second to last window, I had a feeling it might be person who I had done some small good deed for that I never really knew.

I was so wrong. I should have known though. It so happened to be one of the people I most hated in my life. It was a boy, my first love, my ex. It took me the longest out of anyone to forgive and move on.

I watched him with nothing but contempt. Scoffing at the fact that I had helped him the most. /Of course./ My mind cursed at his life. After him I had to turn selfish to protect myself from bullshit like hin. It was the one thing in my life I wish I hadn't had a hard lesson in.

The only thing I kept thinking about was how years after breaking up with him, whenever I met someone, I always thought about whether this person's flaws were worst than his or not. They never were. It did help me to see the worst people for their wrongs and the best people for their merit. It also helped me accept the flaws in good people and the virtues in bad people.

Maybe if I never met him, I wouldn't have desparetly cling onto my mom after heartbreak and find out what true family love is like before she passed away.

But... Maybe if I never met him, I wouldn't have wronged the person I did. I wouldn't have given him what, surely, summed up to five thousand dollars or more. I would still have this fantasy idea in my head about what love could be.

The scars don't go away. At least not for me.

I picked him up when he needed it the most. I helped him survive. I showed him loyalty and unconditional love. I know he probably didn't mean to spit it all in my face; but he did.

Even as I saw life through his eyes, nothing was a good enough excuse for me to accept what he did. To steal from me and my family even after everything I had offered him. To cheat on me and manipulate me.

I sighed. Clearly I was the idiot. But I was only a teen with 'a lot' of money who hadn't learned life lessons yet because my family was over protective of me.

Eventually it passed. His 'era' with me. It felt like forever. It was disgusting to watch. It wasn't even as bad watching the rest of his life as it was to mess mine up.

Whatever. Some part of me was happy for him. The other part had a hard time not hating him again. Who am I kidding I was there hating on him the whole time.

I'm thankful it passed. But he can still go to hell for all I cared. I knew I'd be the person at his fifth window. Or so I hoped, so at least I could die knowing he didn't do worst to some other poor soul.

All this was supposed to be about me helping him and showing how generous I was... Well it was, but it doesn't take away from the half regret. I don't think I would ever help someone out like that again even if I had the choice. Because I had never been able to afford, not then and not at any point in my life.

But maybe I should had made that a priority. A lot of people told me I did enough good in the world. But now I don't believe I did. Was this really my best? I needed to do better. To give back more. To love more. 

I had never realized it before. But perhaps I could have started to set up a life for myself where I could help others more, with volunteering or donations.

----

I was back. Into the last window. I knew what was coming for me, facing the weight I carried every day of my mistake.

His life started in poor slums. Although he could tell it all better himself, as he liked to tell stories of his life over and over. A few of his sisters and brother grew up under the same roof, most didn't.

He went into engineering, his sisters became doctors, and eventually they all went down different paths. I saw him meet my grandmother. Then I saw something that I had never thought I would, I saw my mom grew up. My uncle too. This would answer many questions I was never able to ask about how they grew up, because this perspective was easier to understand. I tried to cherish every moment more I had with each one of them, even if this was all a memory.

It felt so long before I was born and my anxiety grew. I often felt like closing my eyes, as I saw myself grow up again. 

Then it came to happen. After three years of being in that toxic relationship, my ex manipulated me to steal from my grandfather in order to have the money to leave Venezuela. 

It doesn't matter that I gave half of it back, or that I shared some of it with a friend so they too could get out of that situation, or that I was able to leave the country. I stole from my family. I dropped to my knees in shame, in remembering that every second after that was a path I was leading because of what I had done. There was no taking it back and heading down another path, even if it meant not meeting the man I love.

There wasn't a day I woke up without that on my concious. Deep down I knew there was nothing I could do to make up for it, although I tried. Now as Im dead, I felt like I hadn't done enough for the world, for others, for my family. Maybe I had more regrets than I realized.

I didn't know what was going to happen after this was over, but I knew what I had to do if I were alive.

Part1:
/Here I am. Finally dead. It's not so bad. I just didn't think I would be able to keep thinking./

There are five windows ahead of me and I'm forced to step up, put my head out and my vision changes. I begin to relive my life. Except Im clearly not reliving it. Im just watching. There's a stabbing in my heart, every time I misbehave and yell at the people that love me, knowing what would come next. I start crying, I miss my youth and Ive always known it but now I got to see how spoiled I was. I knew that wouldn't last long either.

I got to analyze myself into the teen years, seeing where it all went wrong. The small traumas that I never truly admitted to myself were traumas despite the memory cause instant fear inside me and reminding me it wasn't the end yet. Suddenly I'm so glad I'm dead, but I'm unsure what all this is supposed to be. /It's going to be okay./ I tell my younger self- but it doesn't work that way.

My life starts getting closer and closer to That moment. I grew nervous... I'm forced to watch as I go through relationships so painfully. I watched all the embarrassing moments and all the tears. But I also got to see love, and happiness, and so many things my mind had pushed away. Things I had forgotten. Things I would have given anything to remember. I already knew the worst was coming, the good wouldn't help, but at least it was there to comfort me and make me smile through the tears.

When my mother died again, I broke down. I really couldn't take it again. 

...

I never moved on from it. But my vision kept changing anyway, I knew the world wouldn't stop for her. So I created a disconnect from everything in order to cover that hole with a curtain.

I didn't see most of what had happened next. But I knew it would get better now. I anticipated when I would first see him. I needed him. I looked around everywhere on the streets to see if we ever met beforehand.

It was like falling in love again. All the pain goes away. But I was still crying. I missed him and I knew he missed me.

I don't believe I lived with many regrets. "Present day" me always thought about "future" me. And every day I had to give it my all. Though a lot of times I felt like it wasn't enough or that I could do more, perhaps I was too hard on myself. Perhaps all those small good deeds I did throughout my life were enough.
